sections.h2: How can I sell a house quickly in Jackson, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Jackson owners can list on the open market, sell directly to a buyer they find themselves, or take a cash offer on the house in its present condition. Speed usually comes from the last option, while the first tends to bring the widest pool of buyers.

Jackson is the Madison County seat and the main trade center of West Tennessee, so there is steady demand from workers at the hospital system, schools and distribution employers. The practical choice often comes down to repairs. A house with deferred roof, plumbing or foundation work can sit on the market, while a buyer who pays cash can price those problems in and close on a date you pick.

  • Open market: more showings, more repair requests from buyers' inspectors.
  • Direct sale: lower marketing cost, more paperwork on your side.
  • Cash offer: a single decision, usually with the house sold as is.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Jackson itself?
sections.html:
Jackson is 70 miles east of Memphis and 130 miles southwest of Nashville, and it is known by the nickname Hub City. The settlement began along the Forked Deer River, was first called Alexandria, and was renamed in 1822 for Andrew Jackson. The legislature set up the town in 1821 as a seat of justice, and railroads that arrived from 1851 turned it into a regional hub.

Interstate 40 passes through the city with six exits, and U.S. 45, called Highland Avenue locally, runs north and south. The Keith Short Bypass loops the western side. McKellar-Sipes Regional Airport handles air service, and the Jackson Transit Authority runs city buses.

Children in the city attend the consolidated Jackson-Madison County School System. West Tennessee Healthcare, created by a 1949 act of the General Assembly, is the public hospital system, and the Tennessee Supreme Court holds sessions for West Tennessee here. The Census Bureau lists 58.44 square miles of land and an average commute of 18.2 minutes, shorter than most Tennessee cities of its size. Short drives are a selling point you can mention to buyers.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Jackson housing?
sections.html:
Jackson's estimated population was 69,339 on July 1, 2025, a gain of 1.7 percent from the 2020 base. Just over half of occupied homes are owned by their residents, and values sit well below the Nashville suburbs.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 51.2 percent
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $217,800
  • Median gross rent: $1,145
  • Median household income: $53,032
  • Households: 27,541, with 2.34 people each

Because nearly half of Jackson homes are rented, a large share of buyers in the city are investors. That helps a seller whose house has tenants or needs a rehab, since those buyers expect to do work.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax for a house inside Jackson city limits?
sections.html:
Two offices send separate bills. The City of Jackson Revenue Office collects city tax, and the Madison County Trustee collects county tax. The county's Assessor of Property sets values for both but does not send bills or accept payments.

OfficeWhat it handlesPhone
Assessor of Property, 100 E. Main St., Suite 304Appraisals, value reviews, mailing address changes731-423-6063
Madison County TrusteeCounty tax bills and payments731-423-6027
City of Jackson Revenue OfficeCity tax bills and payments731-425-8210

The assessor says notices should reach owners in the first week of October and that taxes cannot be paid early. It also warns that any tax figure on a closing statement before October 1 is an estimate. Under state law the property stays in the January 1 owner's name on the tax roll for the whole year, so ask your closing attorney how the bill is divided.

sections.h2: When is Madison County's next reappraisal, and how do I appeal?
sections.html:
The assessor has scheduled the next countywide reappraisal for 2027, after the last one in 2022. The office reports a median home sale price of $251,450 as of January 2026, up from $212,500 in January 2022, which it calls an estimated 18.33 percent rise. Owners should expect a notice of value reflecting that change.

Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value. To challenge a value, first call the assessor to verify the property record. If that does not settle it, the Madison County Board of Equalization, five local property owners, hears appeals during the first two weeks of June, and appointments open in the last two weeks of May. The county's page states that taxes for an earlier year cannot be appealed later.

A further appeal goes to the State Board of Equalization by August 1 or within 45 days of the county board's notice, whichever is later. Bring recent comparable sales, a private appraisal if you have one, and photos.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded in Madison County?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Madison County Register of Deeds, 100 East Main Street, Suite 109, on the first floor of the courthouse. Hours are 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, and the phone number is 731-423-6028. The land records go back to 1821, the year Jackson was founded, and the office offers a property alert sign-up.

Madison County's instructions say a deed is stamped before it goes to the Register for recording. Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price, so a sale at the $217,800 Census median value would carry about $806 in transfer tax. A name removal after a death needs the death certificate if the person is on the deed, or a probated will if not, so call 731-423-6063 for that step.

sections.h2: Do I need a permit for work before selling in Jackson?
sections.html:
If the house is inside Jackson city limits, call the City of Jackson Building and Codes Department at 731-425-8262, and also the Madison County Building Department at 731-423-6014. For a house in the county only, call the county department.

The county asks owners to buy permits for remodels, room additions, repairs after storm or flood damage, and new construction so records stay accurate. Unpermitted work on a house you are about to sell can come up when a buyer reviews the property record. Fix or disclose it first.

The Revenue Office on the first floor of City Hall also issues city business licenses, which a landlord selling a rental may have held, and is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Do I pay city and county property tax separately in Jackson?
faqs.a: Yes. Inside city limits you get one bill from the City of Jackson Revenue Office and another from the Madison County Trustee. Outside the city only the county bill applies.

faqs.q: What is the next reappraisal year in Madison County?
faqs.a: 2027. The assessor lists 2022 as the last reappraisal year, and appeals of a yearly value go to the county Board of Equalization during June.

faqs.q: How much is the Tennessee transfer tax on a Jackson home sale?
faqs.a: The state charges $0.37 for each $100 of purchase price. For example, the tax on a $217,800 sale is about $806, and your contract decides who pays it.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Jackson, TN?
faqs.a: At the Madison County Register of Deeds, 100 East Main Street, Suite 109, Jackson, TN 38301, phone 731-423-6028. The office is open 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jackson house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer takes the house subject to the existing lease unless the tenant agrees to leave, and many Jackson buyers are investors who want occupied rentals. Share the lease, deposit amount and rent history with the buyer.
